title: Metabolic Parameters Determination in Acid Citrated Plasma
author: Bianca Hemmeryckx
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j9dcr26

steps.title: Prepare Acid Citrate Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 ml of acid citrate solution (pH 4.5).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 1.25g trisodiumcitrate dihydrate (85 mM, Merck MilliporeSigma Catalog #S1804) and 0.82g citric acid monohydrate (78 mM, Merck MilliporeSigma Catalog #33114) in 20 ml milliQ water.
Add MilliQ water until the final volume is 50 ml.

steps.title: Collect Blood Samples
steps.instruction: Collect blood from the retro-orbital sinus using a capillary tube containing acid citrate.

substeps.instruction: Collect 300μl of blood into an eppendorf tube containing 30μl acid citrate (1/10 dilution).
Discard the first two drops of blood.

steps.title: Isolate Plasma
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood to obtain plasma.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood in an eppendorf centrifuge for 10 min at 10,000 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for Analysis
steps.instruction: Mix plasma with metabolic buffer in a 1 ml sample cup (provided by the routine lab of UZ Leuven, Leuven, Belgium).

substeps.instruction: Combine 50μl of acid citrated plasma with 100μl metabolic buffer (consisting of 0.1 M Tris pH 7.5 and 0.15 M NaCl).

steps.title: Transfer Samples for Measurement
steps.instruction: Transfer samples to the routine lab of UZ Leuven, Leuven, Belgium for measurement of the following plasma levels: total cholesterol, LDL- and HDL-cholesterol, triglycerides, alkaline phosphatases, and aspartate and alanine aminotransferases.
